newsitem.title: USA: McVeigh pal confession details Oklahoma bomb plan.
newsitem.headline: McVeigh pal confession details Oklahoma bomb plan.

text.p: An army friend of bombing suspect Timothy McVeigh said in a confession McVeigh told him he was planning to blow up the federal building in Oklahoma City in the hope of fomenting "some type of general uprising," CBS News reported on Thursday.

In summaries of 1995 confessions to federal officials by Michael Fortier and his wife, Lori, which were first obtained by CBS Dallas affiliate KTVT, the couple said they knew details of the Oklahoma City bombing in advance.
"Tim wanted to wake up America to the danger of our federal government and their intrusions on our rights. He was hoping to accomplish some type of general uprising," he said.

Fortier said he received a letter from McVeigh which indicated he and Terry Nicols decided to "take action," and invited Fortier to help them. McVeigh later revealed he was planning to blow up the federal building in Oklahoma City, according to the confession summaries.
On April 19, 1995, an explosion destroyed the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City, killin 168 adults and children.
Prosecutors in the case had no comment, but two of CBS' sources close to the investigation confirmed the documents' authenticity, the network reported.

A further motive for McVeigh choosing the Murrah building, according to the documents, was that he believed agents and orders that came out of the building were responsible for a federal raid and siege against a compound in Waco, Texas, occupied by followers of David Koresh, which resulted in more than 80 deaths in a fiery showdown.
But McVeigh was mistaken, CBS said, because the raid was planned by the Houston office of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms.

The Fortiers' confession gave several details about how the bomb was to be built and then placed in a truck and detonated. Mrs. Fortier also admitted she assisted McVeigh in preparing a false driver's license with the name Robert Kling -- the same alias prosecutors said was used to rent the truck used for the bomb.

McVeigh's lawyer, Stephen Jones, said the Fortiers' were lying. Michael Fortier faces a 43-year sentence for having advance knowledge of the bombing but not informing authorities. However he is cooperating with prosecutors. Mrs. Fortier was not charged.
The Fourtiers were expected to be star witnesses at the trials. McVeigh and Nichols will be tried separately, with McVeigh first on March 31. Nichols will be tried at a later, undetermined date.
